skill.name: web-perf
skill.description: Audits page speed with Chrome DevTools MCP, traces Core Web Vitals, inspects network bottlenecks, and reviews code for measurable performance improvements.
skill.summary: Profiles page performance and prioritizes evidence-based fixes using Chrome DevTools.
skill.author: cloudflare

security_audit.summary: All 59 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, or Chrome DevTools MCP method names. One separate medium supply-chain risk remains because the setup executes an unpinned latest package.

remediation.issue: The MCP setup executes chrome-devtools-mcp@latest through npx with automatic approval.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact reviewed package version and update it only after reviewing release notes and package provenance.

content.user_title: Audit Web Performance with Chrome DevTools
content.value_statement: Slow pages reduce engagement and hide complex loading bottlenecks. This skill records Chrome traces, evaluates Core Web Vitals, and prioritizes measurable fixes.
actual_capabilities: Records cold-load performance traces through Chrome DevTools MCP.
Reports captured Core Web Vitals and supporting page-load metrics.
Analyzes LCP breakdowns, layout shifts, render blocking, and document latency.
Inspects request chains, payload sizes, caching headers, and critical resources.
Captures accessibility snapshots and flags common high-level gaps.
Reviews supported framework and bundler configurations for optimization opportunities.
limitations: Requires a configured Chrome DevTools MCP server.
Cannot audit third-party source code without codebase access.
Lab traces may differ from real-user field performance.
Accessibility snapshots do not replace complete manual testing.

use_cases.title: Improve a Product Page
use_cases.description: Trace a slow product page and prioritize loading fixes by estimated impact.

use_cases.title: Validate a Performance Release
use_cases.description: Compare captured metrics and network behavior after an optimization release.

use_cases.title: Plan a Site Speed Sprint
use_cases.description: Turn trace evidence into a focused backlog of measurable performance work.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Page Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit {URL} with a cold-load trace. Report key metrics, the top three issues, and specific fixes ranked by estimated impact.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Loading Bottlenecks
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze {URL} for render blocking, request chains, caching problems, and large payloads. Explain the evidence behind each priority.

prompt_templates.title: Review Performance and Accessibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit {URL} for Core Web Vitals and accessibility gaps. Separate measured findings from observations that require manual verification.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Trace Findings to Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace {URL}, inspect the available codebase, and map major bottlenecks to framework or bundler changes with expected impact.

output_examples.input: Audit the home page and identify the largest loading delay.
output_examples.output: LCP needs improvement. The hero image is discovered late through CSS, so preloading and direct markup are the highest-priority fixes.

output_examples.input: Review scripts and styles for avoidable blocking work.
output: High: Defer the noncritical analytics script that blocks first paint.
Medium: Split the route bundle to reduce unused JavaScript on initial load.
Low: Keep the stylesheet because its measured blocking impact is negligible.

output_examples.input: Check performance and high-level accessibility issues.
output_examples.output: Performance is strong, but two controls lack accessible names. Confirm keyboard focus behavior manually before release.

best_practices: Run a cold-load trace before recommending changes.
Verify every issue with trace, network, DOM, or code evidence.
Prioritize fixes with measurable impact and state uncertainty clearly.
anti_patterns: Do not recommend removing resources without confirming they are unused.
Do not treat zero-impact trace observations as priority work.
Do not present lab measurements as real-user field data.

faq.question: What tools does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Chrome DevTools MCP with navigation, tracing, network inspection, and snapshot tools available.

faq.question: Which performance metrics can it assess?
faq.answer: It assesses captured Core Web Vitals and supporting metrics such as FCP, TBT, TTFB, and Speed Index.

faq.question: Can it audit any website?
faq.answer: It can inspect pages reachable by the configured browser. Code-level recommendations require access to the related repository.

faq.question: Does it replace Lighthouse?
faq.answer: No. It uses DevTools traces and insights to provide targeted investigation and implementation guidance.

faq.question: Can it perform a complete accessibility audit?
faq.answer: No. It identifies high-level snapshot issues, while complete validation still requires automated and manual accessibility testing.

faq.question: How are recommendations prioritized?
faq.answer: Recommendations use measured impact, trace evidence, request details, and code context when available.
